papers.title: The enemy of my enemy: A bacterial antagonist rescues Chlamydomonas by inactivating a toxin from a rival
papers.abstract: Microbial interactions are shaped by multiple community members, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated a tripartite interaction between the microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii and two Pseudomonas bacteria that coexist in the same soil habitat. In pairwise cultures, all three interactions are amensalistic (-like): Pseudomonas protegens Pf-5 antagonizes both C. reinhardtii and Pseudomonas fluorescens HKI0770 without benefit, while P. fluorescens inhibits C. reinhardtii without profiting from the alga. However, in a tripartite culture, P. fluorescens protects C. reinhardtii from P. protegens and promotes algal recovery. This protection is not stopped when the used carbon source, acetate, is supplemented. The P. fluorescens rescue effect is associated with reduced levels of the polyyne toxin protegencin produced by P. protegens. Protegencin levels, detected by Raman microspectroscopy, are decreased by application of spent medium or protein extracts from P. fluorescens, while heat- and protease-treatment abolish this activity. A heat-sensitive, proteinaceous factor, likely an enzyme(s), appears to contribute to protegencin inactivation. Our results show that P. fluorescens rescues C. reinhardtii by inactivating protegencin, despite being inhibited by P. protegens. These findings demonstrate the importance of investigating higher-order effects, since additional community members can transform pairwise antagonistic interactions into conditional protection through toxin inactivation.

papers.title: Integrative identification of Tetratostichococcus sp. CCAH0201 (Trebouxiophyceae, Chlorophyta) from Rhizophora leaves in the Can Gio Mangrove Forest, Vietnam
papers.abstract: A microalgal strain from Rhizophora leaves in the Can Gio Mangrove Forest, Vietnam, was examined by light microscopy and three molecular markers. Thirty-six cells from 22 micrographs measured 6.68-12.74 by 3.49-4.79 micrometres. Homologous phylogenetic windows comprised 550 nucleotides for SSU rDNA, 711 for ITS and 1,170 for rbcL. CCAH0201, P1 and Tetratostichococcus jenerensis SAG 2138 shared the SSU 3-prime sequence, whereas ITS and rbcL placed CCAH0201 with P1 (SH-aLRT/UFBoot 87/94 and 96.9/99). CCAH0201 differed from P1 at 22/711 ITS and 4/1,170 rbcL sites. Structure-guided ITS2 comparison identified one strict CBC, one two-sided change from a wobble pair and three hemi-CBCs relative to P1. CCAH0201 is thus identified as Tetratostichococcus sp. in a lineage close to P1.

papers.title: CauloBrowser 2.0: an AI powered update
papers.abstract: CauloBrowser is a systems-biology database for Caulobacter crescentus that organizes the largest repository of experimental data for this model bacterium. The original CauloBrowser provided a web interface for accessing these data, but the growing number of experimental datasets and advances in AI chatbots motivated an updated resource. We developed CauloBrowser 2.0 (CauloBrowser.org) as an open-source application that broadens access to RNA-seq, microarray, ribosome profiling, Tn-seq, ChIP-seq, and genome annotation data. The CauloChat AI interface allows users to query these datasets in natural language, generate visualizations, and achieve complex biological insights. While the database is hosted freely on the web, users may also download the database and run it locally, reducing dependence on the web-hosted service and allowing laboratories to use compatible unpublished datasets. Altogether, CauloBrowser 2.0 provides a significant update for exploring diverse systems biology data in C. crescentus.

papers.title: Creation of genomic chimeras via megabase scale genome expansion
papers.abstract: An organism's physiology is controlled by its genomic content. Building genomic chimeras would enable melding of the diverse functions and properties of life. However, prior arts in genome synthesis are limited to reconstituting pre-existing functions within a singular genome rather than combining diverse genomic functions across multiple distinct genomes. Existing methods are also prohibitively expensive, labor intensive, and time consuming, and thus fundamentally not scalable for creating large synthetic chimeric genomes. To address all these limitations, we invented Additive Conjugative-CAST Engineering (ACE) combining conjugation with CRISPR-associated transposition (CAST) to deliver and integrate up to half a genome per step from a donor cell into a precisely defined position in the recipient's genome. We have demonstrated ACE's capability to integrate at least a 2-megabase donor genomic segment in a single step and at least 3 megabase in two consecutive steps. Importantly, we confirmed ACE's generality through the creation of multiple genomic chimeras across species, genus, and at least order barriers. With ACE, we further demonstrate such chimeric organisms, or what we call genome expanded organisms (GEOs), can be stably forged from at least three starting bacterial strains, and can be stably maintained to express all their acquired genomic parts in a single chimera. ACE offers a new paradigm of creating artificial lifeforms to combine desired properties and potentially create novel functions beyond the constraints of nature. ACE also offers a unique perspective to probe unexplored plasticity in genome architecture and expression patterns of novel, massively expanded genomes.

papers.title: Rates of molecular and morphological evolution are uncoupled across the eukaryote Tree of Life
papers.abstract: A vast degree of phenotypic variation can be seen across lineages of eukaryotes. Although at least part of this diversity has a genomic basis, it is unclear whether there are broad-scale links that can be detected between rates of genomic and phenotypic evolution. The presence of a correlation would imply the action of shared drivers, such as mutational or adaptive processes that occur on a genome- and organism-wide scale. We investigated this question by using a phylogenetic approach to test for correlations between molecular and morphological evolutionary rates. We analysed 60 data sets of combined nucleotide sequences and discrete morphological characters, representing a diverse range of eukaryotes that include alveolates, plants, invertebrates, fishes, and tetrapods. Using a maximum-likelihood phylogenetic approach based on sister-pair contrasts, we found very little evidence of any link between rates of molecular and morphological evolution, a striking result given the scale and taxonomic breadth of our analyses. Our results point to contrasting evolutionary dynamics underlying genomes and phenotypic traits, most likely involving differing extents of selection. These processes have also led to greater variation in morphological evolutionary rates across lineages, whereas molecular evolution is more clocklike. Our results have implications for how evolutionary change should be modelled in phylogenetic analyses of combined data sets. Overall, our study reveals the discrepancies in evolutionary drivers that act at the genomic and phenotypic levels across the eukaryotic Tree of Life.

papers.title: Signatures for conserved phenolic-based acclimation responses to UV in a unicellular algal sister of land plants
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) light is a major stressor that particularly comes to bear in the terrestrial habitat. As such it is among the major challenges that the earliest land plants had to overcome. The closest algal relatives of land plants, the zygnematophytes, are single celled and filamentous algae that - in the context of their terrestrial and freshwater habitats - have diverse adaptations to UV irradiance. As such, contextualized with data on land plants, zygnematophyte algae harbor important information for inferring how the earliest land plants have acclimated to UV. Here we exposed the unicellular zygnematophyte model Mesotaenium to daily UV irradiance and assessed its response through microscopy, untargeted metabolomics, and global gene expression profiling using transcriptomics. Our data reveal cell biological acclimation by formation of lipid droplets. Further, we find that the cells accumulated chemodiverse coumarin-like derivatives. Altogether, our data suggest that acclimation to long-term UV exposure is composed of building blocks of a molecular chassis conserved with that of land plants, underpinned by phenolics and genes that are tied to their biosynthesis. From this chassis, divergent evolutionary trajectories have assembled them into a divergent conformation - one of which ushering in the emergence of the phenylpropanoid pathway.

papers.title: Tracing the Evolutionary Histories of Human Cholinergic Proteins Across Eukaryotes: A Comparative Phylogenomic Study
papers.abstract: Acetylcholine signalling depends on a coordinated network of enzymes, transporters, and receptors whose evolutionary histories need not be congruent. Here, we examined 26 curated human cholinergic reference proteins across 89 selected eukaryotic proteomes using a human-reference-anchored phylogenomic framework. Candidate sequences were identified through sequence similarity searches and evaluated using domain architecture, orthology assessment, and family-level phylogenetic analyses. Gene-tree/species-tree reconciliation was performed for selected datasets to investigate putative duplication and loss histories. The results revealed heterogeneous patterns among the investigated protein groups. CHAT- and SLC18A3-associated candidates were recovered across multiple sampled bilaterian lineages, whereas SLC5-family-related sequences showed broader representation, including sampled ctenophores, cnidarians, and bilaterians. Within the latter group, a distinct vertebrate-associated subgroup was identified in relation to human SLC5A7. Cholinesterase analyses recovered an echinoderm-associated grouping and distinct vertebrate ACHE- and BCHE-associated groups, although their deeper evolutionary relationship received comparatively lower support. Muscarinic and nicotinic receptor analyses recovered selected subtype- and subunit-associated groupings, but limited taxonomic representation and sequence instability constrained broader evolutionary interpretation. Collectively, these findings reveal heterogeneous taxonomic distributions and phylogenetic relationships among proteins corresponding to the human cholinergic system. The study provides a comparative framework for examining these protein groups while emphasizing that their recovered evolutionary histories must be interpreted in the context of reference-sequence selection, taxonomic sampling, and phylogenetic resolution.

papers.title: Breaking the bottleneck: semi-automated quantification of actin filament dynamics
papers.abstract: Actin reconstitution assays visualized by total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy have been crucial for defining mechanisms of filament assembly, disassembly, and higher-order organization. Yet quantitative analysis remains slow, labor-intensive, and subject to investigator bias. We developed SMAUG (Single filament Measurement and Analysis Using a GUI), a semi-automated image analysis interface that extends TSOAX filament segmentation and tracking with user-verified trace analysis of time-lapse TIRF images. SMAUG generates kymographs and quantifies filament nucleation, elongation, pausing, junctions, and filament-associated fluorescence while retaining measurements at the individual filament level. We tested the approach across actin reconstitution assays producing concentration-dependent polymerization, formin-stimulated elongation, capping-induced arrest, Arp2/3 branching, and fascin-mediated bundling. SMAUG reproduced manual measurement while reducing analysis time and revealed where dense networks and bundled filaments require user validation. Together, TSOAX and SMAUG provide a semi-automated approach for quantitative analysis of actin filament dynamics.

papers.title: Transition Fibers Play a Central Role in Import of a Glucose Transporter into the Flagellar Membrane
papers.abstract: Leishmania parasite promastigotes have a motile flagellum that encompasses a variety of integral membrane proteins, but how such proteins traffic selectively to the flagellum is largely unknown. The flagellar-specific glucose transporter, GT1, binds to the KHARON protein via the transporter hydrophilic amino terminal domain, and KHARON is essential for trafficking of GT1 from the flagellar pocket membrane at the base of the flagellum into the flagellar membrane. A major objective of this study was to determine the mechanism whereby KHARON transports GT1 into the flagellar membrane. We have determined that KHARON is a novel component of the transition fibers that project from the basal body at the base of the flagellum toward the flagellar membrane. We propose that KHARON binds GT1 at the transition fibers and then transfers it to intraflagellar transport (IFT) trains as they enter the flagellum at this site. The IFT trains, associated with the membrane tethering protein TULP, then move GT1 through the transition zone filter into the body of the flagellum. These results provide evidence for a role for transition fibers in transport of membrane proteins into flagella.

papers.title: Genomic features and instability of linezolid resistance in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis ST525
papers.abstract: This study investigated the mechanisms of oxazolidinone resistance and genomic background in clinical ST525 Enterococcus faecalis isolates, a poorly characterized lineage reported in Brazilian hospitals as either vancomycin-resistant (VRE) or linezolid- and vancomycin-resistant (LVRE). Five LVREfs from intensive care unit patients (linezolid MICs, 8-32 mg/L; vancomycin MICs, >256 mg/L) carried only G2576T and G2505A (in three of four rrl copies) as known linezolid resistance determinants, despite variable linezolid MICs. During serial in vitro passages without antibiotic pressure, isolates with initial MICs of 8-16 mg/L exhibited progressive MIC reductions accompanied by reversion of mutant to wild-type rrl copies, whereas the isolate with an initial MIC of 32 mg/L maintained high-level resistance without reversion. Additional domain V substitutions emerged during MIC decline, while growth kinetics remained broadly similar. Whole-genome sequencing of a representative isolate (LVREfs L7) revealed a ~2.8-Mb chromosome enriched in mobile genetic elements (~8.6%), lacking a functional CRISPR-Cas system. A plasmid-borne prototype Tn1546 carrying vanA, devoid of internal insertion sequences, was found inserted into a Tn3-family transposase gene, a platform not typically associated with vanA mobilization. Together, these findings indicate that ST525 LVREfs, whose genomic features are consistent with long-term persistence in hospitals, may pose a challenge to routine susceptibility testing. A single mutational mechanism can yield variable linezolid MICs, and the ratio of mutated vs wild-type rrl copies can become heterogeneous in the absence of antibiotic pressure, without correlating directly with these values, contrary to the well-documented copy number-MIC correlation.

papers.title: Targeting REV1 Exposes Context-Dependent Therapeutic Responses in Colorectal Cancer
papers.abstract: Translesion synthesis (TLS) promotes DNA damage tolerance and contributes to chemotherapy resistance by enabling replication across damaged DNA templates. REV1, a central TLS regulator, is a potential therapeutic target to enhance the efficacy of genotoxic chemotherapy. Here, we investigated the therapeutic consequences of pharmacologic and genetic REV1 targeting in colorectal cancer (CRC) and evaluated the sensitivity of patient-derived CRC organoids to the REV1 inhibitor JH-RE-06. JH-RE-06 enhanced oxaliplatin sensitivity in HCT116 cells and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) sensitivity in HT-29 cells, whereas reciprocal combinations produced limited sensitization, indicating treatment- and cellular context-dependent responses. siRNA-mediated REV1 depletion similarly enhanced chemotherapy sensitivity, supporting REV1 involvement in these responses. MNNG sensitivity assays and MLH1 expression analyses did not reveal consistent treatment-associated changes in mismatch repair function, while targeted HPRT1 sequencing identified no detectable sequence alterations in the region examined. Chemosensitization was not accompanied by consistent increases in caspase-3/7 activation under the conditions tested. REV1 inhibition also caused LC3-II accumulation and, after prolonged inhibitor exposure, reduced beta-tubulin abundance, indicating additional autophagy-associated and cytoskeletal responses. In two patient-derived CRC organoid models, JH-RE-06 exhibited single-agent growth-inhibitory activity, with mean IC50 values of 2.01 micromolar and 1.4 micromolar, respectively. Together, these findings demonstrate context-dependent chemosensitization and organoid growth inhibition following REV1 targeting, suggesting that its therapeutic consequences may extend beyond canonical TLS-mediated DNA damage tolerance.

papers.title: Mutant Isocitrate Dehydrogenase 1 Alters Extracellular Vesicle Secretion and Cargo Composition in Cellular Models
papers.abstract: Somatic mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) define major subtypes of adult diffuse gliomas and occur across a broad spectrum of cancers. These mutations ablate the conventional turnover of isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutarate and confer the neomorphic production of D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D2HG), which drives epigenetic remodeling. Growing evidence suggests this neomorphic activity may also affect how tumor cells communicate; small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are elevated in gliomas, though how mutant IDH1 shapes sEV production and cargo remains poorly understood. Using glioblastoma and chondrosarcoma cell models, we show expression of mutant IDH1 correlates with a trend of increased sEV secretion, and that D2HG is packaged into sEVs that are taken up by cells. Cell-permeable D2HG treatment dose-dependently increased sEV release from IDH1 wild type cells. Untargeted proteomics showed that mutant IDH1 expression remodeled sEV cargo in a cell type-specific fashion, with mutant chondrosarcoma sEVs enriched in one-carbon metabolism enzymes, and mutant glioma sEVs in lysosomal luminal proteins and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperones. Mutant IDH1 glioma cell transcriptomics suggested expanded ER folding capacity and reduced ribosomal pathways, and sEVs from these cells decreased nascent protein synthesis in IDH1 wild type recipient cells. Together, this suggests sEVs can serve as carriers of mutant IDH1 phenotypes.

papers.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Tumorigenic Lineages and Interactions Persisting and Evolving From Premalignancy to Cancer in the Stomach
papers.abstract: Background & Aims Gastric cancer is often diagnosed at advanced stages, making the premalignant window critical for early detection. However, the epithelial changes that characterize this stage remain poorly defined. We used CTLA4-knockdown (CTLA4KD) mice, which model human CTLA4 insufficiency-associated gastric cancer, that develops autoimmune gastritis, metaplasia, and adenocarcinoma, to define molecular changes across disease progression. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing and 40-color spectral flow cytometry were performed on gastric tissue across premalignant and cancer stages. We evaluated epithelial lineage relationships, cell-cell communication pathways, and candidate markers at the transcript and protein levels in murine and human gastric adenocarcinoma. Results We identified a metaplastic/tumorigenic population in CTLA4KD mice that emerged in premalignancy with a chief cell transcriptomic origin. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed a progressive increase in fibronectin (FN1) signaling from premalignancy through cancer, transitioning from stromal to autocrine signaling in the metaplastic/tumorigenic population. Expression of Embigin (EMB), a fibronectin receptor, increased at both transcript and protein levels in premalignancy and remained elevated in cancer. EMB epithelial cells co-expressed CD133, a cancer stem cell marker, consistent with a stem-like phenotype. EMB expression was also higher in human gastric adenocarcinoma than in matched normal tissue. Conclusions Using a model that captures the full histopathological cascade of gastric tumorigenesis, we delineate single-cell transcriptional programs that persist and evolve from premalignancy to adenocarcinoma. In-depth computational analyses identified novel markers involved in cell-cell communication during tumorigenesis, including EMB, an epithelial marker that persists from premalignancy through cancer in the murine model and validated in human gastric adenocarcinoma, suggesting EMB as a marker of premalignant progression.

papers.title: Continental scale genetic diversity supports geo-clustered ecoregions connectivity
papers.abstract: Connectivity is fundamental to ensuring that ecosystems can recover after impact. The genetic information in DNA metabarcoding can provide insight into connectivity at different timescales. We compared structural connectivity, represented by an adjacency matrix of ecoregions, and functional connectivity at different levels of organization, represented by the {beta}-diversity of exact sequence variants and species, between ecoregions, focusing on benthic arthropods. While structural and functional connectivity were correlated, there was a distinct divide between eastern and western ecoregions that approximately aligned with the Rocky Mountains. Within the western ecoregions, species {beta}-diversity was not correlated with ecoregion adjacency and had higher intraspecific genetic differentiation. This implies that gene flow is more restricted in this area. Understanding how gene flow can be limited is important to conservation planning.

papers.title: An expanded evolutionary landscape of H3 histones with variants that destabilize nucleosomes and promote chromatin accessibility
papers.abstract: Histones are among the most conserved proteins in eukaryotes, yet many animal lineages have evolved divergent histone variants with specialized functions. Some broadly conserved variants (e.g., H3.3) have been linked to the regulation of chromatin accessibility in stem cells, but whether highly divergent variants function similarly remains unclear. Here, we characterize the histone repertoire of the acoel Hofstenia miamia, an animal that can undergo whole-body regeneration using adult pluripotent stem cells (aPSCs). We identify two novel histone H3 paralogs, H3-a and H3-b, that are expressed in aPSCs and form a lineage-specific sister clade to H3.2 and H3.3. Despite substantial sequence divergence and reduced compatibility with canonical chaperone machinery, both variants assemble bona fide nucleosomes in vitro. These nucleosomes exhibit reduced stability and incomplete DNA wrapping, and a cryo-EM structure of the H3-b nucleosome reveals the disruption of conserved histone-DNA contacts. In vivo, H3-a and H3-b are upregulated following injury, and their depletion reduces genome-wide chromatin accessibility, suggesting a role in the maintenance of accessible chromatin during regeneration. A survey of H3 sequences across animal phyla shows that H3-a and H3-b belong to a broader landscape of highly divergent H3 proteins, some of which exhibit sequence differences across both the N-terminal tail and histone-fold domain. Together, these findings link histone sequence diversification to chromatin regulation in aPSCs and highlight the underappreciated evolutionary diversity and functional potential of divergent animal H3 proteins.

papers.title: SOPSim: A cell vertex-based application for simulating sensory bristle patterning with dynamic filopodia
papers.abstract: Repeating patterns, such as the bristles on the thorax of fruit flies developed from sensory organ precursor (SOP) cells, play important roles in the lives of flies as they are connected to the central nervous system and help detect environmental cues and threats. Notch signaling is known to regulate the formation of these patterns. Primarily, Notch signaling involves local communication between neighboring cells in direct contact (apical or junctional interaction). However, this short-range interaction alone cannot fully explain the complex biological patterns observed. Further studies have revealed long-range communication between cells through actin-based protrusions known as filopodia. The precise understanding of how the dynamics of filopodia, such as protrusion and retraction, lead to Notch-Delta activation remains unclear, which limits our ability to fully comprehend the mechanisms underlying cell fate decisions and the emergence of spatially organized patterns during tissue development and regeneration. In this study, we extend the modeling framework for Notch signaling by incorporating a filopodia dynamics model driven by myosin-mediated contraction. We address existing gaps by defining criteria under which any given pair of filopodia will physically intersect. We also introduce the local sensory area (LSA), a metric for quantifying local SOP spacing, and use experimental data to calibrate a Notch threshold that distinguishes SOP from epithelial cells. Through numerical simulations, we confirm that long-range communication via filopodia is essential for reproducing the refined patterns observed in vivo. Additionally, we explore how filopodia length, lifetime, and orientation influence the spatial organization of SOP cells. To this end, a Python library has been developed which allows users to perform simulations of Notch Delta signaling via a (1) Graphical User Interface/website, local to the user's computer, (2) via commands in the command line interface, or (3) by calling the simulation using a function via a Python API. This library allows users without computational expertise to easily specify a small number of input parameters and generate simulations of the model.

papers.title: Regenerative epithelial spike cells instruct immune niche homeostasis in zebrafish fin epidermis
papers.abstract: Epithelia comprise diverse specialized epithelial cells that interact with immune cells, yet how these interactions sustain immune cell pools remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis with transgenic assays in zebrafish and discovered a previously unrecognized epithelial population marked by advillin (avil). We identified epithelial cells exhibiting unique morphology and localization, characterized by an apical spike projecting outward from the body - which we term spike cells. These cells exhibit features reminiscent of mammalian tuft cells. Notably, avil+ spike cells exhibit close spatial association with a subset of mpeg1+ immune cells. Following fin amputation, spike cells are replenished de novo from precursors and undergo dynamic changes in density, morphology, and orientation, and their regeneration depends on Alk signaling. Moreover, spike cells dynamically interact with mpeg1+ immune cells to maintain the immune cell population. Together, our findings identify a unique epithelial population in zebrafish fins and define their roles in maintaining immune cell niche dynamics.

papers.title: A multipotent mouse distal airway secretory cell population that contributes to both airway and alveolar regeneration
papers.abstract: The distal airway is a spatially distinct compartment whose contribution to lung repair remains poorly defined. We have identified an epithelial cell population enriched in the most distal airways of the mouse lung, that is not present in the alveolar epithelium. Using lineage tracing tools based on Cldn10 expression which marks these cells, we show that the Cldn10+ lineage in homeostatic conditions marks distal airway secretory cells in a highly specific manner, with only a small contribution to multi-ciliated cells and no contribution towards the basal stem cell lineage. Remarkably, these Cldn10+ distal secretory cells proliferate and display a high degree of multi-potency across the lung epithelial axis after injury, generating basal cells, multi-ciliated cells, and alveolar epithelium. In severely remodeled regions after injury, we show that Cldn10 lineage-labeled cells migrate from the airways and differentiate into alveolar epithelial cells. These findings establish the Cldn10 lineage that defines a distal airway secretory facultative progenitor with both intrapulmonary airway and alveolar potential, providing a genetic system for studying distal lung repair.

papers.title: Multicellular Perturb-seq Reveals Lineage-Specific Transcriptional Control During Human Cardiac Organoid Development
papers.abstract: Heart development requires the coordinated differentiation of multiple cell lineages, including cardiomyocytes (CMs) and endothelial cells (ECs). Transcription factors (TFs) orchestrate lineage specification, morphogenesis, and maturation, yet how cardiac and vascular TFs shape multicellular organization and their interactions remain poorly understood. Many TFs exhibit pleiotropic and stage-dependent effects across cardiac lineages, particularly in cardiac progenitor cells, suggesting the presence of shared regulatory networks that synchronize cardiac and vascular programs during development and in response to stress. Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) differentiated cardiac organoid provides a physiologically relevant 3D model to study these multicellular interactions, enabling simultaneous differentiation of ECs and CMs within a human genetic context. When combined with CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) based Perturb-seq, this system allows systematic, high-throughput dissection of TF-driven regulatory programs at single-cell resolution. In this study, we investigated how cardiac and vascular TFs coordinate lineage commitment and the cross-lineage signaling in human cardiovascular differentiation.

papers.title: Persistent and recyclable myosin II minifilaments drive cortical contractility in the early C. elegans embryo
papers.abstract: Non-muscle myosin II is a key regulator of cell and tissue morphogenesis, yet the cortical dynamics of myosin minifilaments in vivo remain poorly understood. Here, we combine SIM-TIRF and single-molecule TIRF microscopy to characterize the structure and dynamics of myosin minifilaments in an early developing embryo. High-temporal-resolution SIM-TIRF imaging revealed diverse minifilament behaviors, including partition-like events, long-range alignment of multiple minifilaments into collective structures we called proto-stress fibers, partial unbinding, and sequential unbinding and rebinding to the cortex. Photoconversion experiments showed that minifilaments persist as intact units after cortical unbinding, diffuse through the cytoplasm, and can be recycled over long distances rather than disassembling upon detachment. Despite these dynamic behaviors, minifilaments are predominantly stationary when bound to actin. Numerical simulations demonstrated that this static behavior is essential to sustain cortical stress within a continuously remodeling actin network. Using myosin motor-domain mutants, we further investigated the contribution of motor activity to these behaviors. Together, our results reveal that myosin minifilaments can persist as stable units while cycling between the cortex and cytoplasm, and that their predominantly static behavior when bound to actin enables sustained force generation in a continuously renewing cortical network. These findings provide new insights into myosin organization, recycling, and force generation during early embryonic development.

papers.title: Optogenetic induction of TAD boundary pairing promotes gene activity
papers.abstract: The genome folds inside the nucleus into distinct structures across multiple levels of organization. Topologically associating domains (TADs) are a ubiquitous architectural feature of genomes delineated by boundaries enriched in the CTCF protein and the cohesin complex. TADs are dynamic structures as their boundaries undergo continuous, short-lived pairing events. Whether the structural integrity of TADs contributes to regulation of the genes within the TAD is unclear. To directly test the structure-function relationship of TADs, we have developed OptoTet, an optogenetic tool to rapidly and directly manipulate chromatin contacts in a controlled fashion using light without the need for mutation or protein depletion. Using the TADs containing the ERRFI1 or MYC gene as model systems, we show that OptoTet promotes TAD boundary looping. When applied to probing the structure-function relationship of TADs, light-induced pairing of TAD boundaries promoted transcriptional activity of ERRFI1 as indicated by increased gene bursting. In contrast, bursting of MYC was insensitive to boundary pairing. Enhanced TAD boundary pairing also partially rescued the effect of depletion of cohesin components on ERRF1 but not on MYC. Our results suggest that TADs boundary pairing dynamics can contribute to gene regulation in a gene-specific manner.

papers.title: Stepwise assembly and mechanical stability of nsP3 Helical Scaffolds in Chikungunya Virus
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA virus that replicates its genome through a viral replication complex (RC) essential for successful infection. The RC consists of four non-structural proteins: nsP1, nsP2, nsP3, and nsP4. In this study, we focused on nsP3, which comprises three distinct domains: the alphavirus unique domain (AUD), the long and intrinsically disordered hypervariable domain (HVD), and the enzymatic macrodomain (MD). Notably, nsP3 assembles into helicoidal macrostructures, termed helical scaffolds (HSs), which are components of the CHIKV replication complex and are involved in the formation of macromolecular traps in the cytoplasm of the infected cell called Alphagranules (AGs). HSs form tubular helical scaffolds assembled through the AUD, with the MD and HVD flexibly deployed to the scaffold exterior. Despite their functional importance, the mechanisms governing HS formation remain poorly understood. Using High-Speed Atomic Force Microscopy (HS-AFM) and Electron Microscopy (EM) we achieved new findings on the structure, mechanics and assembly of these macrostructures. Our results show the nsP3 monomers follow intermediate steps before completing the assembly into full helical scaffolds, with each nsP3 domain contributing differently to this process. The macrodomain (MD) provides mechanical stability, yet it fractures under tens of piconewtons of force. This rigidity acts as a mechanical regulator that constrains the position of the HVD, which in turn mediates interactions with host factors and neighboring HSs. Through this interplay, nsP3 achieves both structural cohesion and functional adaptability, promoting the higher-order organization of HSs into honeycomb-like networks.

papers.title: Global repression of mesenchymal genes in epithelial cells by the histone demethylase LSD1
papers.abstract: Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is an essential process in development, tissue repair, and tumour metastasis, and is triggered by SNAI, ZEB and TWIST transcription factors, that recruit lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) to repress epithelial genes such as E-cadherin. In mesenchymal cells, LSD1 inhibition restores E-cadherin expression and reduces migration and invasion, consistent with LSD1 inhibition reverting EMT, and offering a therapeutic modality for EMT-associated disease. Recent data, however, suggest context-dependent roles for LSD1, as its inhibition in epithelial cells increases mesenchymal marker expression, potentially promoting EMT. To investigate this discrepancy, we mapped genome-wide binding of LSD1 in HCT116 epithelial cells and used rapid degron-mediated ablation of endogenous LSD1 to measure changes in nascent and steady-state transcription and chromatin accessibility. In epithelial cells, LSD1 binds constitutively-accessible, primed mesenchymal promoters. These are rapidly derepressed after LSD1 ablation, with activation of SNAI2 and ZEB1, which repress epithelial hallmarks such as E-cadherin. Re-introduction of LSD1 downregulates SNAI2 and ZEB1 but, surprisingly, further represses E-cadherin, indicating sustained loss of epithelial characteristics. Collectively, our results show that LSD1 maintains epithelial identity by repressing mesenchymal genes, questioning the therapeutic utility of LSD1 inhibition for EMT control.

papers.title: Stoichiometric Encoding of Amplification Kinetics Enables High-Level Multiplexing in Single-Channel TaqMan Real-Time PCR
papers.abstract: Multiplexing in TaqMan real-time PCR (qPCR) is limited to four-six targets per reaction by fluorophore spectral overlap. Amplification curve analysis (ACA) can discriminate several targets within one fluorescence channel from amplification curves (AC) kinetic features, but has been confined mainly to digital qPCR (dqPCR) and is sensitive to domain shifts between instruments and specimen types. Here, we co-design biochemical encoding of target-specific information into ACs and their computational decoding to achieve single-channel 8-plex TaqMan qPCR on a standard thermocycler. Using asymmetric PCR, we show that forward primer, reverse primer and probe concentrations act as a programmable encoding mechanism, generating a 27-condition design space of reproducible non-canonical ACs, conserved from digital to bulk qPCR. Applying this stoichiometric encoding to an 8-plex central nervous system pathogens panel increased inter-target separability, raising the mean silhouette score from 0.329 to 0.711. To decode ACs without labelled target-domain bulk qPCR data, we pretrained a transformer encoder by self-supervised learning on more than 170,000 unlabelled dqPCR curves and aligned source and target domains using conditional domain adversarial training. On contrived clinical specimens, the framework classified a canonical 7-plex respiratory virus panel with 83.6% accuracy (versus 67.7% for a supervised baseline) and the encoded 8-plex panel with 89.8% accuracy. Furthermore, stoichiometric encoding enabled resolution of double- and triple-target co-amplification events with 98.7% accuracy in controlled dqPCR experiments. This approach expands the information capacity of existing qPCR instrumentation without new hardware, fluorophores or oligonucleotides, offering a low-cost route to syndromic molecular diagnostics.

papers.title: Metatranscriptomic Profiling of Viral Diversity in Aquatic Environments with a Focus on Microalgal Viruses
papers.abstract: Freshwater microeukaryotes contribute to aquatic productivity, yet the RNA viruses associated with these communities remain incompletely characterized compared with their marine counterparts. Here, we used metatranscriptomics to profile viral diversity across five Finnish freshwater sites (one river and four lakes) and one coastal marine sample from Hiroshima Bay in the Seto Inland Sea, Japan. We recovered 399 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs), of which 285 (71.4%) represented RNA viruses distributed across five viral phyla and putatively associated with fungal, plant or algal, metazoan and bacterial hosts. DNA viruses formed a smaller component of the dataset, including bacteriophage-like vOTUs with transcripts encoding replication, structural, packaging, and lysis proteins. Two vOTUs, which were detected in the Vantaanjoki river sample, were putatively classified within the family Marnaviridae, which comprises RNA viruses that infect protists in marine and freshwater environments. Both vOTUs encoded conserved replication and picornavirus-like capsid domains, and one represented a near-complete dicistronic genome. RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) -based phylogeny placed these vOTUs in a strongly supported lineage outside the currently recognized genera within the family Marnaviridae, supporting their provisional assignment to the candidate genus Vandarnavirus proposed here within Marnaviridae. Whole-genome comparisons using the IMG/VR v4 database revealed genetic similarities between the vOTUs representing the candidate Vandarnavirus genus and picorna-like virus sequences from freshwater, wetland, saltmarsh, and estuarine metatranscriptomes. These findings expand the known ecological range of marnavirus-like RNA viruses and identify freshwater habitats as under-sampled reservoirs of microalgae-associated viral sequences.

papers.title: Evaluating non-oxidative glycolysis using 13C metabolic flux analysis
papers.abstract: Non-oxidative glycolysis (NOG) converts glucose to acetyl-CoA without emitting CO2 during Escherichia coli bioproduction. Although 13C-metabolic flux analysis (13C-MFA) has the potential to evaluate NOG flux distribution in vivo, the precision of these estimates depends on the labeling patterns of glucose tracers. Because E. coli has multiple native glycolysis pathways, selecting the optimal glucose tracer is important for precise estimates. This study used simulations to evaluate the performance of 18 commercially available glucose tracers in precisely predicting NOG flux. We artificially generated flux distributions of central metabolic pathways, including three types of NOG pathways, and obtained 13C labeling patterns of amino acids metabolized from each glucose tracer. Using these data, we then calculated 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for NOG pathway fluxes. Comparing the sum of CI widths from three NOG fluxes showed that estimation with [1,3-13C]-glucose yielded the narrowest CIs. Several tracers, including [2,3-13C]glucose, were capable of determining fluxes with high precision, but [1-13C]glucose was not one of them, despite often being used for estimating glycolytic fluxes. We then experimentally evaluated [2,3-13C]- and [1-13C]glucose as tracers in E. coli strains with and without the expression of phosphoketolase, which is required for NOG pathways to function. The results suggested that [1-13C]glucose could not detect NOG fluxes, whereas [2,3-13C]glucose estimated the fluxes of all three NOG pathways with narrow CIs.

papers.title: Visual surfaceomics reveals the substrate-scavenging cell surface of Asgard archaea
papers.abstract: The emergence of eukaryotes from Asgard archaeal ancestors likely required a specialized cell envelope that enabled sustained physical and metabolic interactions with proto-mitochondrial symbionts. While the protrusion-rich cell architecture of Asgard archaea may enable such interactions, the molecular composition of their cell surface and its role in establishing cell-cell contacts remains unknown. Here, we developed a "visual surfaceomics" approach, integrating subtomogram averaging, predictive structural modeling, transcriptomics, proteomics, and expansion microscopy to identify surface proteins in situ. We show that Asgard cell bodies and protrusions lack an archaea-typical paracrystalline S-layer and are instead decorated by two main classes of surface proteins: subtilisin-like serine proteases (SubSs) and oligopeptide-binding proteins (OppAs). SubSs were detected as membrane-anchored dimers and were sparsely distributed across the surface. OppAs showed near-total membrane coverage but lacked any rigid, higher order assembly. Thermal shift assays and single particle cryo-EM showed that OppA binds oligopeptides in vitro. Comparative genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics suggest that this peptidophilic surface architecture is conserved across Asgard archaeal phyla. Finally, we discovered that the cell surface was remodeled at cell-cell contact sites. Altogether, our integrative approach revealed a metabolically specialized and structurally flexible cell surface that couples extracellular protein degradation with peptide capture and uptake, while potentially contributing to establishing and maintaining the symbiotic interactions of Asgard archaea.

papers.title: Genomic signatures distinguish isolates of Salmonella Typhimurium from humans and livestock
papers.abstract: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium is a major cause of human salmonellosis and livestock represent an important reservoir for human infection through the food chain. However, it remains unclear whether isolates recovered from human disease reflect the broader livestock population or constitute a subset of livestock-associated isolates characterized by specific genetic features. Here, we analysed 1,398 S. Typhimurium genomes from human, poultry, bovine and swine isolates to evaluate whether isolates associated with human disease can be distinguished from those circulating in livestock and to identify the genetic features underlying this discrimination. Whole-genome multilocus sequence typing profiles were converted into a gene presence/absence matrix and analysed using four machine-learning algorithms, which showed high and consistent discriminatory performance. Model performance was influenced by the phylogenetic structure of the population and by the variable distribution of human- and livestock-associated isolates across lineages of sequence type (ST) 19, the most prevalent S. Typhimurium ST. Nevertheless, within ST19, 97 genes were significantly enriched and 36 were significantly depleted in human-associated genomes relative to genomes from each of the three livestock sources. Human-enriched genes included 14 genes required for biosynthesis of the lipopolysaccharide core, the O-antigen, the T1 antigen, and six virulence factors. These genes were consistently absent from livestock-associated genomes across ST19 lineages. Conversely, human-depleted genes included the galactitol utilisation cluster and five virulence genes, which are predominantly absent in specific ST19 lineages. Overall, our findings support the existence of host-associated genomic signatures that distinguish isolates associated with human disease from those sampled from the livestock reservoir.

papers.title: UVC Irradiation Induces Time-Dependent Proteomic Remodeling in Geodermatophilus obscurus G20
papers.abstract: Geodermatophilus obscurus G20 is a multi-resistant extremophile observed to survive significant dosages of ultraviolet (UV) radiation. Despite previous work having measured G. obscurus G20s proteome in relation to its genome sequence, its proteomic response to stressors has yet to be explored. This study utilizes bottom-up proteomics with data independent acquisition to derive comprehensive proteomic measurements in both healthy and two UV-stressed conditions induced through 254 nm UV radiation administered at a median lethal dose. The first, an acute response treatment group, was recovered and flash-frozen immediately after UV radiation. The second, a recovery response treatment group, was allowed to incubate for 1 hour following UV radiation. Gene enrichment analysis revealed an increase in NADH dehydrogenase activity among both stressed treatment groups, however the recovery response treatment group experienced additional changes including reduced peptidoglycan synthesis and increased translational activity. Results suggest that the repair process undergone by G. obscurus G20 persists well after initial UV exposure and is likely to be inducing noteworthy energetic demands to facilitate UV induced genomic repair. Proteomic analyses revealed patterns that advance our mechanistic and temporal understanding of the G. obscurus metabolic response to UV irradiation.

papers.title: Geometric Morphometrics of Pistillate Flowers in Astrocaryum sect. Huicungo (Arecaceae): Taxonomic Implications for the Peruvian Species
papers.abstract: The taxonomy of the Amazonian palm clade Astrocaryum sect. Huicungo remains controversial due to deep discordances between traditional classifications based on qualitative floral traits and recent phylogenomic evidence. To address this, landmark-based two-dimensional geometric morphometrics (4 landmarks, 16 semilandmarks) was applied to evaluate the symmetric component of shape variation in calyx and corolla structures across 549 pistillate flowers from the 11 Peruvian species. Although multivariate analyses (PCA, CVA) revealed continuous morphological variation and extensive phenotypic overlap, perianth geometry retained a significant diagnostic signal. Cross-validated classification rates demonstrated that the corolla exhibited higher discriminatory power than the calyx, while the combined perianth analysis (calyx + corolla) maximized taxonomic assignment accuracy. Furthermore, Mahalanobis distance-based clustering did not replicate traditional subsections: A. chonta and A. ulei exhibited divergent architectures, whereas A. carnosum, A. faranae, and A. huicungo shared profound geometric similarity. This study demonstrates that quantitative perianth morphometrics is a valuable tool for species delimitation in Astrocaryum, supporting the re-evaluation of traditional taxonomic boundaries through an integrative approach.
